findings.text: Externally visible reopen operation that attempts to take back the newest log descriptor for the same originator and prepare its message storage for extension.
Externally visible publish operation that moves a reservation toward committed visibility and finalizes it when a newer head already exists.
Caller supplies ring, scratch record, originator tag and size bound; success yields usable message storage and reservation state, failure clears the scratch record and reports false.
Caller supplies an initialized reservation; the call publishes it and closes the interrupt masked window, with a possible followup transition to finalized.

Descriptors move among reserved and committed and finalized and reusable, with miss for absent; reopen expects committed by same originator back to reserved, commit moves reserved to committed, finalization moves committed to finalized, reclamation moves finalized to reusable.

Message formatting first renders variable arguments into supplied space, then drops one trailing line break while recording that fact in flags, then removes any leading severity prefix when no facility was given, then emits a console trace and returns the remaining length.
Originator tag distinguishes non task context, where it uses the current task numeric identity, from task context, where it combines a base offset with the current processor number.
One build variant records originator tag and task name into the info object, while an alternate build variant leaves the info object untouched.

Empty requests produce dataless markers without storage; non empty requests are rounded to block granularity, head is advanced atomically after ensuring tail room, the new area is tagged with the record identity, and wrap cases redirect payload to ring start while still tagging both locations.

Growth is allowed only for the newest block; unchanged or shrinking sizes reuse the current payload location, larger sizes push tail and advance head atomically, and transition into wrapping copies prior payload to ring start.

Tail advancement marks overlapped finalized descriptors reusable after verifying backward linkage, retries when another party moved tail concurrently, and fails when blocked by absent or still active descriptors.
End position computation keeps non wrapping blocks contiguous and maps wrapping blocks to start at the current wrap base plus size, with payload stored at ring start.
Dataless blocks account zero; contiguous blocks account index distance; wrapping blocks also include trailing wasted space.

Finalization progress is tracked by scanning forward from last known finalized sequence through readable valid records and publishing the furthest found value with release ordering, retrying on concurrent updates.

Reopen reserve path masks local interrupts on entry and restores the saved state exactly once on every exit, either through the shared commit helper on failure or through commit completion on success.

Head, tail, head identity and descriptor state are mutated only with atomic read and compare exchange loops plus documented acquire release and barrier pairing, allowing concurrent writers and reclaim without a central spin lock in these fragments.

Observed relationships link ring to descriptor ring and text data ring, reservations to ring plus identity plus saved interrupt state plus used space, records to info plus buffer plus size, descriptors to state plus text location, and data blocks to owner identity plus payload.
Stored message length is treated as untrusted: dataless blocks expect zero and oversized values are clamped to the real block size with a one time warning before allocation decisions.

Allocation and tail push failures are signaled with dedicated dataless markers or null storage and a cleared scratch record; commit helper warns if the descriptor is no longer in the expected reserved condition.
A data position whose least significant bit is set denotes absence of payload.
Descriptor state word combines record identity with lifecycle state shifted by a shared shift amount.
